jobs.title: Product Owner Cloud
jobs.description:

While you might not have heard of us (yet) over 36,000 accounting and audit professionals list Caseware as a skill on their LinkedIn profiles!

You work closely with a full team—both functional and development—so affinity with both is important. jobs.title: Staff / Senior Product Manager, Payments
jobs.description:
About Airwallex

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

 

About the Role

As a Senior / Staff Product Manager, you will play a defining role in shaping the future of global money movement, embedded commerce, and unified payment acceptance at Airwallex. Operating at the intersection of core clearing/settlement infrastructure, merchant-facing experiences, and developer-first toolkits, you will own the end-to-end product lifecycle—from long-term strategy and architectural design to global roadmap execution.

In this role, you will bridge our online payments-for-platforms suite (enabling marketplaces and SaaS platforms to collect, route, and embed payments) with next-generation in-person commerce (smart POS, SoftPOS, hardware/software integrations, and loyalty engines). You will lead cross-functional teams to modernise omnichannel workflows, scale coverage across international markets, and deploy AI-native capabilities that remove operational friction for global merchants.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the vision, roadmap, and delivery plans for Airwallex’s platform payments and in-person commerce solutions, expanding our reach across key verticals, marketplaces, and global geographies.

  • Architect seamless integrations connecting POS terminal workflows and embedded platform checkouts directly to core clearing, ledgering, and multi-currency settlement engines—optimising for processing speed, fee netting, and dynamic routing.

  • Build developer-first APIs, unified commerce SDKs, and intuitive terminal management systems (TMS) that drastically reduce integration overhead for marketplaces, platforms, and third-party software vendors.

  • Pioneer AI workflows and autonomous agents across merchant onboarding, automated terminal setup, dispute/risk management, transaction reconciliation, and proactive loyalty/reward engine optimisations.

  • Expand capabilities around alternative payment methods (APMs), card acquiring, and integrated loyalty redemption loops to help platforms monetize payments and retain underlying sellers.

  • Ensure high-availability infrastructure (including offline POS processing resilience) while delivering tooling to help merchants satisfy regulatory mandates (PCI-DSS, EMV, PSD3/local frameworks) and manage platform risk.

  • Partner closely with Engineering, Hardware/Firmware, Commercial, Legal/Compliance, and Operations teams to build scalable feedback loops and launch high-impact products from concept to global scale.

Who You Are

Minimum Requirements

  • 5+ years of product management experience building high-scale, mission-critical platform products in fintech, payments, or commerce infrastructure (Staff-level scope).

  • Hands-on domain expertise in card acquiring, embedded finance/platform payment models (marketplaces, payfac-like setups), or card-present ecosystems (POS/SoftPOS, EMV/NFC standards, terminal management).

  • Proven ability to engage deeply with engineering on complex architectural discussions covering API design, distributed ledgers, high-throughput transaction processing, and hardware/software interfaces.

  • Exceptional analytical rigor with a track record of structuring complex ecosystem workflows, leveraging data to drive strategic trade-offs, and solving ambiguous problems.

  • High agency, persistence, and an entrepreneurial bias for action—capable of executing fast and driving complex initiatives to completion in a high-growth environment.

  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills; proven success influencing cross-functional teams and executive stakeholders across diverse international regions.

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher with strong academic performance, preferably with coursework in Computer Science, Engineering, or quantitative disciplines.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience designing or scaling developer-first payment APIs, unified commerce SDKs, or multi-sided platform architectures.

  • Hands-on exposure to deploying Generative AI, agentic workflows, or automated intelligence in fintech operations, transaction reconciliation, or onboarding.

  • Working familiarity with international card networks, alternative payment methods (APMs), cross-border settlement rails, and regional regulatory frameworks (UK/EU, APAC, or Americas).

Applicant Safety Policy: Fraud and Third-Party Recruiters

To protect you from recruitment scams, please be aware that Airwallex will not ask for bank details, sensitive ID numbers (i.e. passport), or any form of payment during the application or interview process. All official communication will come from an @airwallex.com email address. Please apply only through careers.airwallex.com or our official LinkedIn page.

Airwallex does not accept unsolicited resumes from search firms/recruiters. Airwallex will not pay any fees to search firms/recruiters if a candidate is submitted by a search firm/recruiter unless an agreement has been entered into with respect to specific open position(s). Search firms/recruiters submitting resumes to Airwallex on an unsolicited basis shall be deemed to accept this condition, regardless of any other provision to the contrary.

Equal opportunity

Airwallex is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and anyone seeking employment at Airwallex is considered based on merit, qualifications, competence and talent. We don’t regard color, religion, race, national origin, sexual orientation, ancestry, citizenship, sex, marital or family status, disability, gender, or any other legally protected status when making our hiring decisions. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager – Managed Detection and Incident Response (m/f/x)
jobs.description:
About Eye Security

Eye Security is providing cybersecurity with embedded cyber insurance solutions for organizations in Europe. Headquartered in the Netherlands, we are already over 190 FTEs and continue to grow internationally having secured our Series C funding of €60 Million!

We combine cutting-edge technology with hands-on expertise to detect, respond to, and recover from cyber threats in real time. Our team brings together talent from intelligence, military, tech, and consulting backgrounds — all united by a shared mission: to make enterprise-grade cybersecurity accessible to every business, not just the big players.

At Eye, you'll work on projects with an international footprint, solving real-world challenges and helping to build a safer digital future for our clients.

About this role

As our client base continues to grow rapidly across Europe, this role will play a key strategic part in scaling our Managed Detection and Response (MDR), Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), and Incident Response (IR) capabilities.

You'll take full ownership of the product strategy and roadmap for this space. Collaborating with our engineers, product designers, security operations, product marketing, and cross-functional leadership, you will ensure that our platform evolves with our customers' needs and delivers maximum impact at scale.

This is a senior individual contributor and thought leadership role designed for someone who thrives on autonomy, discovery, and leading cross-functional product development in a fast-growing environment. You'll be the strategic voice shaping our product direction, mentoring product managers, and influencing broader company strategy.

What you will do

  • Own and communicate the long-term product vision and strategy for MDR, EDR, and IR. Define strategic priorities, influence company OKRs, and drive cross-functional alignment around product direction.

  • Define and own the product roadmap for MDR, EDR, and IR, ensuring alignment with company vision, market opportunity, and customer needs.

  • Drive discovery practices to deeply understand customer needs, problems, and pain points.

  • Lead and mentor product managers and junior team members. Work closely with Engineering, Product Design, Security Operations, Product Marketing, Customer Success, and Sales to deliver successful outcomes and build high-performing teams.

  • Partner with Product Marketing to define comprehensive go-to-market strategies, product launches, and market positioning that drive competitive advantage.

  • Manage external relationships and partnerships, especially with EDR vendors and MDR technology providers, ensuring alignment with our MSP and partner strategy.

  • Stay at the forefront of cybersecurity trends, emerging technologies, and industry best practices.

  • Contribute to the evolution of our internal processes, tooling, and product culture. Champion agile methodologies, data-driven execution, and continuous experimentation.

What you will need

  • 7+ years of Product Management experience, with at least 4 years in senior or staff-level roles owning end-to-end delivery of software products in B2B SaaS or similar environments.

  • Deep cybersecurity domain expertise.

  • Proven track record of successfully delivering complex software products in fast-paced environments using product discovery, data-driven decision making, and agile methodologies.

  • Strong business acumen: understanding of go-to-market strategy, sales enablement, and how product drives revenue and customer success.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to present complex strategies clearly to technical, commercial, and executive audiences.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving mindset, with comfort in ambiguity and the ability to make sound decisions with incomplete information.

  • Fluent English

Nice-to-have

  • Startup or scale-up background at a high-growth company.

  • Experience building or scaling product management teams and processes.

  • Exposure to OKR-driven product development and metrics-focused product management.

  • Experience working with MSP or partner-led go-to-market models.

  • Track record of navigating successful product pivots or strategic repositioning.

What we offer

  • A meaningful mission: protect organizations across Europe from real-world cyber threats.

  • Work with top-tier professionals from national CERTs, intelligence agencies, and leading tech backgrounds.

  • Full strategic ownership of a mission-critical product area in a high-growth cybersecurity scale-up.

  • Mentorship and growth: lead and develop the next generation of product managers; grow into broader strategy and leadership roles.

  • Weekly lunches (NL) and Thursday socials to stay connected.

  • A generous time-off policy, including wellbeing and volunteering days.

  • Competitive salary and benefits package, including equity participation.

Are you up for it?

We look forward to receiving your application.

We are an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to making our hiring process accessible to everyone. If you need a reasonable accommodation to apply or interview for this role, please inform the TA team.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Core Product
jobs.description:
About us

Founded in 2019 and part of Y Combinator's 2020 cohort, Photoroom is the leading visual solution for e-commerce.

We've raised Series B funding and reached 300+ million users worldwide, processing over 5 billion images annually and serving both small businesses and major enterprises like Amazon, DoorDash, and Decathlon through our mobile app, web platform, and API.

We're a team of 100+ passionate builders giving e-commerce businesses superpowers to create visuals that help them grow, making the hardest parts of selling online disappear. We focus on craft, innovation, and collaboration to create exceptional impact for e-commerce businesses worldwide.

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the self-serve product experience for our SMB customers: small to medium brands selling on Shopify and beyond. The proposition for this segment is unbuilt, the squad is yours to shape, and you'll own the slice of ARR that comes with it. Working closely with engineers, designers, and AI researchers, you'll decide what gets built, why, and how it ships

Location: Paris, hybrid 3 days in the office. We offer relocation support

About the role

  • Own a real slice of the self-serve product. From idea to shipped feature, you will build and execute the roadmap that solves problems for our users.

  • Define the problem before the solution. Sharpen the user problem, then partner with design and engineering to ship work that feels effortless.

  • Turn AI capabilities into products people want. Work hand-in-hand with our researchers and engineers to convert new model capabilities into shipped features that move usage and revenue.

  • Stay close to the user. Talk to e-commerce sellers every week, and feed what you hear directly into roadmap decisions.

  • Use data to decide, not to justify. Pull and interpret data yourself, form hypotheses, measure what shipped, and call what's next. You won’t need to wait around for someone else to run the query.

About You

  • You've shipped products you can defend in detail. Five+ years as a PM, with multiple launches where you can name the user problem, what you owned personally vs. the team, and the measured outcome.

  • You've built B2B SaaS for self-serve customers. You know the mechanics of self-serve growth, retention, and pricing, not just enterprise sales cycles.

  • AI has reshaped how you work. You use Claude or equivalent every day, for prototyping, testing with users, or automating the parts of the job that used to fill your calendar. The value you bring sits in strategy and direction, not in writing tickets.

  • You have demonstrable product taste. You can show specific work where the details matter and explain the calls you made, including the ones you'd make differently now.

  • You create clarity from ambiguity. Given a fuzzy problem, you take action rather than waiting for direction: you structure it, decide what matters, and move.

  • You're data-fluent. You pull, interpret, and challenge data yourself, and use it to form a point of view rather than confirm one.

  • You thrive in small teams with high autonomy. You can ship without being managed, and can operate in a fully remote, async-first environment that offers no scaffolding around you.

Nice to have: experience building creative tools or any product where craft and visual quality matter; an understanding of photography or videography; entrepreneurial experience (you've started, built, or run something).

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging

We're committed to enabling everyone to feel included and valued at work. We believe our company and culture are strongest when composed of diverse experiences and backgrounds.

That's also why we have flexible working hours, trust people to work in a hybrid environment, and extended parental leave.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, SMB e-commerce Growth
jobs.description:
About us

Founded in 2019 and part of Y Combinator's 2020 cohort, Photoroom is the leading visual solution for e-commerce.

We've raised Series B funding and reached 300+ million users worldwide, processing over 5 billion images annually and serving both small businesses and major enterprises like Amazon, DoorDash, and Decathlon through our mobile app, web platform, and API.

We're a team of 100+ passionate builders giving e-commerce businesses superpowers to create visuals that help them grow, making the hardest parts of selling online disappear. We focus on craft, innovation, and collaboration to create exceptional impact for e-commerce businesses worldwide.

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager, SMB E-commerce Growth to own activation, monetization, and retention for our SMB e-commerce segment across the Photoroom mobile and web apps. This is a growth role: you'll own the levers that turn sign-ups into retained subscribers, and the growth-led features that move them. From paywalls to pricing experiments and onboarding and discovery flows, you'll partner closely with User Acquisition on the handoff from paid to product, and with the core SMB product team on what gets built next.

Location: Paris, we offer relocation support (Hybrid

About the role

  • Own a real slice of the growth funnel. Activation, paywall, pricing, or retention: you'll lead a squad and own a specific number end-to-end, deciding what gets tested, what gets built, and what gets killed.

  • Move the metric, not just the backlog. Run a high-velocity experimentation program across web and mobile funnels. Ship A/B tests weekly, and bigger feature bets when the data calls for them.

  • Find the insight, then build the feature. The best growth work is spotting why users drop off and shipping the change that fixes it. You'll do both.

  • Work across web and mobile. Mobile and web funnels behave differently (App Store vs. card-on-file, push vs. email). You'll own both, and partner closely with the User Acquisition team on the handoff from paid to product.

  • Use data to decide, not to justify. Pull and interpret data yourself, form hypotheses, measure what shipped, and call what's next. You won't need to wait around for someone else to run the query.

About You

  • You've moved real numbers on a subscription product. Five to eight years as a PM, with concrete activation, monetization, or retention wins you can name with the KPI, the change, and the percentage impact, owned by you, not by a team you sat on.

  • You've worked on something with recurring revenue. Whether B2B SaaS, B2C subscription, or B2B2C, as long as your work was tied directly to revenue your experience will give you a leg up. Pure marketplace or pure free-product backgrounds will struggle here.

  • You know how SMB sellers buy. You understand how SMB e-commerce sellers discover, evaluate, and adopt utility SaaS, the kind of motion behind Shopify, Canva, Klaviyo, Stripe, Klarna, Gorgias, Recharge, Loop, Wix, or Squarespace.

  • You think in funnels. You understand activation curves, paywall psychology, trial design, and the difference between credit-based, feature-gated, and seat-based pricing, and you have opinions on which works where.

  • You build with AI. You use Claude or equivalent to automate recurring tasks, and can explain how you set it up to help you ship faster.

  • You're data-fluent. Comfortable with SQL and an analytics platform like Amplitude or Mixpanel; you build and interpret your own funnel without waiting for a data scientist, and you've shipped a high volume of A/B tests personally in the last 12 months.

  • You thrive in small teams with high autonomy. You can ship without being managed, and can operate in a fully remote, async-first environment that offers no scaffolding around you.

Nice to have: experience on both web and mobile funnels; familiarity with the Shopify ecosystem (app store, connect flows, merchant personas) or a comparable e-commerce platform; entrepreneurial experience (you've started, built, or run something).

If you think you have what it takes but don't meet every single point above, please still apply. We'd love to chat and see if you could be a great fit.

jobs.title: Fractional Product Lead - 3 month contract
jobs.description:
We're customer obsessed. We put the customer at the heart of everything we do - and we're looking for people who feel the same way.

About Bike Club

Bike Club is the easiest way to keep kids on the right sized bike. Through our subscription model, we remove the hassle of buying, outgrowing and reselling children's bikes, so families always have the right bike, right when they need it. We are a purpose led, fast-growing business built on ease, care, progress and joy - with a relentless focus on customer growth, retention and building a more circular approach to children's cycling.

Role Summary and Engagement

Bike Club is looking for a fractional Product Lead to lead the member product, turn customer needs and commercial priorities into a clear direction and a prioritised roadmap, and deliver measurable improvements. The role combines senior Product leadership with practical discovery and delivery coordination in a lean team.

The Product Lead will also establish an AI-enabled Product function, using AI to speed up customer insight, discovery, prototyping and experimentation. They will identify where AI and automation can improve the member experience or business efficiency, and turn the strongest opportunities into prioritised, measurable initiatives.

This is a part-time fixed-term employment or freelance contract estimated at 3 days per week for a period of 3 months.

Key Responsibilities

  • Product direction and roadmap: own the direction and roadmap across the member lifecycle: joining, managing a subscription, ongoing membership, exchange and retention. Balance member value with operational efficiency, cost and business priorities.

  • Discovery: lead discovery with members and colleagues across Marketing, Customer Service, Operations and markets. Use research, behavioural data and service insight to define problems before committing to solutions.

  • Lifecycle and retention: work jointly with Marketing and the retention owner on lifecycle journeys, retention initiatives, experiments and shared measures. Product owns the supporting experience and requirements. Marketing owns campaign and channel execution.

  • Requirements and backlog: turn agreed priorities into clear requirements, user stories and acceptance criteria. Maintain one prioritised product backlog, including operational improvements and approved AI or automation initiatives.

  • Investment cases: build proportionate cases for investment, setting out expected benefits, cost, dependencies and how outcomes will be measured. Recommend stopping or deferring work where value is insufficient.

  • Delivery: agree delivery commitments with Engineering using realistic estimates and available capacity. Coordinate stakeholders, adoption and launches with the combined QA and Delivery role, keeping risks and changes visible.

  • Marketing autonomy: support Marketing with appropriate content, landing-page and experimentation capabilities. Agree the boundary between the member product, CRM and support tools.

  • AI in Product work: use AI routinely for research synthesis, analysis, requirements development, prototyping and experiment design, and validate findings against customer evidence.

  • Prioritise valuable applications with Marketing, Customer Service, Operations and the Data and Automation function. Test assumptions and build proportionate business cases. Customer-service automation should support the wider member journey.

  • Share responsibility with Marketing for using AI to support lifecycle insight, proposition testing and retention experiments, with agreed measures of customer and commercial impact.

  • Leave things in a better state: because the engagement is part-time and time-limited, document the roadmap, backlog, ways of working and AI approach so the team can continue without the Product Lead, and hand over clearly at the end.

Requirements

  • Extensive Product Management experience including owning a digital product roadmap and delivering measurable customer and commercial improvements, preferably in a subscription, membership or related consumer business.

  • Strong discovery skills, including customer interviews, journey mapping, data interpretation, problem definition and testing assumptions before investment.

  • Commercial judgement: can compare value, effort, cost and risk, build practical investment cases and make clear prioritisation decisions.

  • Ability to lead across functions, challenge senior stakeholders constructively and maintain focus when priorities compete.

  • Experience working with Engineering, Design, Marketing, Customer Service and Operations through delivery, launch and continuous improvement.

  • Demonstrable experience embedding AI into Product workflows, with examples of faster learning, better decisions or reduced effort. Able to distinguish valuable AI applications from features that add unnecessary complexity.

  • Track record of working independently and effectively in a part-time, fractional or interim capacity, making visible progress in limited days a week.

  • Able to start quickly, and leave behind clear documentation and repeatable ways of working.

Measures Of Success

Baselines, numerical targets, data sources and review dates are agreed with the executive sponsor and relevant business owners within the first 30 days. Delivery and outcomes are reviewed weekly.

  • Member retention: improvement in the agreed retention or cancellation measure for targeted journeys, assessed jointly with Marketing and the retention owner.

  • Member experience: improvement in self-service completion and reduction in avoidable support contact for prioritised journeys, without deterioration in customer experience.

Mission

Turn operational needs, customer feedback, and product direction into clear product specifications—and then drive those capabilities through decisions, design, development, and validation.

You will work directly with the Head of Product on Legion and become a core contributor to both defining the product and running the process around it.

What You’ll Own

  • Create clear, detailed product specifications for new features and capabilities.

  • Take customer needs, operator feedback, technical constraints, and product direction and turn them into actionable product requirements.

  • Own bounded features from early definition through design, development, feedback, and validation.

  • Work directly with Product Design to translate specifications into detailed workflows and Figma designs.

What Great Looks Like

You are given a problem such as:

“Operators need a better way to understand and respond to vehicle health issues during degraded communications.”

You meet with the relevant operators, engineers, customers, and stakeholders.

You understand the underlying problem.

You separate customer requests from actual product requirements.

You identify edge cases and unresolved decisions.

You write a product specification that clearly explains the intended behavior, workflows, system states, requirements, and open questions.

You work with Product Design to turn that specification into a strong interface.

You incorporate feedback, resolve ambiguity, and keep the feature moving until the capability works as intended.

The Head of Product provides direction and reviews the most important decisions—but does not need to personally produce every artifact or manage every follow-up.

Initially, you may draft sections of specifications or own smaller, well-bounded capabilities with guidance from the Head of Product.

We are not looking for someone who spends six months observing before contributing.

The Person We’re Looking For

You are an excellent writer.

You can take a complicated conversation and turn it into a clear product definition.

You have strong product judgment and are comfortable making reasonable decisions when requirements are incomplete.

You understand that a customer request is not automatically a product requirement.

You are technically curious and capable of participating meaningfully in discussions with software engineers, systems engineers, operators, and external partners.

You naturally ask questions like:

  • Who needs this capability?

  • What should happen in this edge case?

  • What does the operator see?

  • What state is the system actually in?

  • How will we know this works?

  • Is this a product decision, an engineering decision, or a customer preference?

  • You are highly organized, but organization is a means to an end.

  • Your real job is creating clarity and moving product decisions forward.

Particularly Valuable Experience

Experience with any of the following would be especially valuable:

  • Technical product management

  • Complex B2B software

  • Aerospace or defense

  • Robotics or autonomous systems

  • Mission planning

  • Geospatial software

  • Systems engineering

  • Government programs

  • Operational testing

  • Requirements development

What This Role Is Not

This is not a project coordinator role.

It is not a Scrum Master role.

It is not an administrative Product Operations position.

It is not someone whose primary contribution is scheduling meetings, maintaining Jira, or writing meeting minutes.

Those activities may occasionally be necessary, but they are secondary.

The primary contribution is:

understanding product problems and defining excellent solutions.

Success After 90 Days

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.description:
Wanna join the adventure?

At Loft, we are convinced that space programs should not have to be rebuilt from scratch every time. Our philosophy has been to productize them: we develop our own proprietary technology blocks, hardware and software, so that a customer payload can be integrated faster and more reliably than any bespoke program allows. That approach has delivered — it is why our customers reach orbit in months rather than years, and it is what makes working here different from working in the rest of the industry.

We are now taking the next step: launching and operating our own constellations, and building a new set of services on top of them. That includes a full product suite enabling third-party AI applications to run directly onboard our satellites, and a growing ecosystem of partners whose needs we have to understand and design for. Loft is expanding at a very high pace, and the range of what we build is expanding just as fast.

This is why Product Management matters so much here. Someone has to hold the whole picture — what is technically possible, what customers actually need, what we should build first — and turn it into something engineering and leadership can act on. As a Product Manager, you will own a significant perimeter and the autonomy that goes with it. We are growing the team precisely so that each of us can go deeper on our topics, anticipate rather than react, and have more impact across the company.

You will need to be comfortable talking to anyone here. In the same week you might sit with a system engineer to understand a design constraint, join a BD call with an institutional customer, and present a recommendation to the executive team. Ideas at Loft get discussed openly and on their merits, wherever they come from, so being able to ask a naive question without ego — and to disagree with someone senior without making it personal — matters more than seniority.


About this role:
Understand what is possible, and turn it into requirements
  • Spend the bulk of your time with engineering: understanding architectures, constraints, and dependencies well enough to judge what is realistically doable in a given timeframe.
  • Translate strategic direction into clear requirements and use cases that engineering can act on directly, and follow them down to the Jira tickets.
  • Surface and shape the good ideas that come from engineering — many of the best ones do — and connect them to a product rationale.
  • Define success criteria for each capability, and verify they are actually met through implementation and delivery.
  • Maintain an accurate, shared view of Loft's product capabilities, what is in development, and where the gaps are.

    • Bring the outside in

    • Run customer discovery interviews alongside business development, and debrief missions to see how Loft's capabilities are actually used in operations.
    • Engage directly with the partners building on our platform, including the onboard AI application ecosystem, to understand their needs and constraints.
    • Track market trends and competitive moves closely enough to know where our offering stands.

      • Decide and prioritize

      • Own the roadmap for your perimeter, reconciling customer needs, engineering reality, and Loft's strategy into a single coherent plan.
      • Build the analysis behind every recommendation — sizing, segmentation, business cases, operational data — so decisions are grounded in evidence rather than intuition alone.
      • Negotiate scope and delivery commitments with engineering leadership, and re-plan when capacity or mission timelines shift.
      • Challenge, constructively and with data, business development, engineering leadership, and your own assumptions.

        • Communicate

        • Own internal communication on your perimeter: keep engineering, program leadership, and executives working from the same technical reality.
        • Develop the technical narratives and proof points that marketing and BD then turn into their own customer-facing material.
        • Prepare recommendations and presentations for top-executive-level audiences.

Must Haves:
  • 7+ years of professional experience, including hands-on product management.
  • Domain experience in at least one of: earth observation, embedded systems, aerospace systems, security & defense.
  • Comfort at both ends of the spectrum — understand the market, and the technology
  • Structured and data-driven: you bring your experience and your intuitions, but when you put a recommendation on the table you can show the analysis it stands on.
  • Real product obsession: you think about the bigger picture and product-market fit before you think about features.
  • Relentless curiosity. In a single month you might move from a satellite bus constraint, to onboard AI inference, to a defense accreditation requirement — and you need to find that stimulating rather than exhausting.
  • High autonomy and a bias for action: handed a broad perimeter, you organize it yourself and come back with a plan.
  • At ease being challenged, and challenging others, in a fast-moving and demanding environment.
  • Working knowledge of both hardware and software development lifecycles.
  • Proficient using and configuring Atlassian tools (Jira and Confluence).
  • Fluency in English, written and spoken.
  • Willingness to travel to other Loft offices and to customers.

Nice to Haves:
  • Fluency in French.
  • Experience with AI/ML products, edge computing, or developer and partner platforms and ecosystems.
  • Experience with satellite operations, constellation services, or ground segment products.
  • Exposure to institutional and defense customers and their procurement cycles.

OUR MISSION

To become the car-changing destination of choice. By combining technology, media and deep automotive expertise, we've turned how people buy, sell, advertise and lease cars on its head.

What started as a simple reviews site is now one of the largest online car-changing destinations in Europe. Last year alone we grew over 50% with nearly £3bn worth of cars bought on site, while £1.8bn of cars were listed for sale through our Sell My Car service.

In 2024 we went big and acquired Autovia - creators of AutoExpress and Evo magazines - doubling our audience overnight. Together we now have one of the biggest YouTube channels in the world with almost 10m subscribers and over 1.1 billion annual views, while we sell 1.2 million print copies of our magazines and have an annual web content reach over 350million.

And we’re a long way from done!

THE ROLE

Buying and selling a car should feel like one seamless motion for a dealer, not two separate systems. Right now it's the opposite: a dealer buys through us, then has to manage collection, payment and resale largely on their own, stitching together workflows across multiple platforms and channels, much of it manual.

For a dealer, speed is money. Every extra day a car sits before it's collected, priced, and paid for is a day of depreciation, tied-up capital, and a missed chance to buy the next one.If we can get a dealer from 'I've bought this car' to 'it's ready and paid for' faster through transport and collections, quicker final pricing, and Wallet, we make them more profitable. A dealer who's more profitable because of Carwow has little reason to go elsewhere: they'll lean on us more, and churn less.

This role owns that last-mile agenda: getting cars collected quickly, resolving final price without friction, and making Wallet work the way dealers expect it to. This team sits across our ambitions to make car changing a seamless journey, this role's job is the handover itself: the operational moment between buying and being ready to sell again. This is also a moment where AI changes what's possible. Dealers are already asking for smarter scheduling, less manual chasing, and tools that reduce the overhead of running a business. We want to build those things. The PM in this role will need the curiosity to explore what that could look like, and the rigour to distinguish genuine value from noise. If you want to own an operational product area end to end, work with some of the most sophisticated buyers in UK retail, and build things that have a direct line to commercial outcomes, this is it.

jobs.title: Technical Product Manager, Integrations
jobs.description:
Who we are

Foundation models transformed text and images. Structured data - the largest and most consequential data format in the world - stayed untouched, until now. What LLMs did for language, we're doing for tables.

We pioneered tabular foundation models: TabPFN v2 was a Nature cover story, has passed 3.5M+ downloads and 7,500+ GitHub stars, and runs in production from detecting lung disease with Oxford Cancer Analytics to preventing train failures with Hitachi. The hardest problems - millions of rows, real-time inference, entirely new modalities - are still open, and no one else is working on them at this level.

We're a small, highly selective team of 40+ with backgrounds from Google, DeepMind, Meta, Apple, Amazon, Jane Street, and CERN, led by Frank Hutter, Noah Hollmann, and Sauraj Gambhir, and advised by Bernhard Schölkopf and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun.

In July 2026, less than 18 months after our €9M pre-seed, we joined SAP as an independent frontier AI lab - same team, mission, and open-weights models, now backed by more than €1 billion over four years.

The role

Most enterprises will never call our API directly. They will meet TabPFN inside the platforms they already run: SAP, AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Databricks, or their own cloud. How well that works, how fast each release arrives there, and which platforms come next is the job of our Technical Product Manager for Integrations.

You take each model release from handover to live across every channel, working with the engineers who build the model and the partner teams who host it. Inside SAP you carry the product side of TabPFN across its platforms, from AI Core to SAP Analytics Cloud, and you help build the integration engineering team that will work with you. Several decisions are yours to bring to the table: which announced channels we build next, what a marketplace listing should cost, how support for all of this works.

You work directly with our product team, our engineers and the founders, and you report to the CTO. This suits someone who enjoys landing things on a date as much as deciding what to build, and who still likes being close to the code.

What you'll do

  • Take every model release live across SAP, the cloud marketplaces and customer environments, on a plan you build with product and engineering.

  • Be the technical counterpart for the partner teams that host TabPFN, from SAP's platform teams to the hyperscaler marketplaces.

  • Shape how TabPFN shows up inside SAP's stack and what the integration engineering team builds first.

  • Bring the open channel decisions to the founders with a recommendation, and stay hands-on: listings, docs, smoke tests, a PR when it is faster than asking.

What we're looking for

  • Two or more years as product manager for a platform or integration surface: a product that ships into partners' platforms, or that other companies build on.

  • You have shipped through gates you did not control, landed multi-team releases on dates, and made a large enterprise's process work for a small, fast team.

  • You started as an engineer and never fully stopped: you read code, logs and scan reports without a translator.

  • You are in Berlin or ready to relocate; Freiburg or New York can work.

What sets you apart

  • You have shipped into an SAP, Salesforce, Microsoft or Oracle ecosystem, or know the cloud marketplaces from the inside.

  • You have deployed machine learning models and know what GPUs cost.

  • You have worked at a startup, and you use AI tools to take real work off your plate.

Life at Prior Labs

You'll work alongside researchers and builders who hold themselves to a very high bar - in the quality of their work and in how they work with each other. We move fast and still take the time to do things right.

Our teams are based in Berlin, Freiburg, and New York - when you're working on something as hard as TabPFN, being in the same room matters. But great people come from everywhere, and in exceptional cases we're open to remote, which usually means frequent travel to one of our offices. Wherever you're based, the whole company comes together regularly for offsites to build and celebrate together.

Our Commitments

The best products and teams are built by people with a wide range of perspectives and backgrounds. We welcome applications from all identities and walks of life - especially if you've ever felt discouraged by "not checking every box" - and provide equal opportunities regardless of gender, sexual orientation, origin, disability, or any other trait that makes you who you are.

jobs.title: Product Lead
jobs.description:
About Abound

We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. While traditional lenders rely almost entirely on credit scores, we look at the full financial picture - how much you spend, and what you can afford to repay to build a deeper, more accurate understanding of each customer's unique financial situation.


And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch.


Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us.

The Role

We are hiring a Product Lead to own our Express / Mid-prime personal loan product, one of our highest-priority growth areas. This is unsecured personal lending in the higher-APR mid-prime space (30% to 50% APR), with loans typically from £2,000 to £10,000, and customers acquired primarily through price-comparison and aggregator marketplaces. Our ambition is to grow this product many times over while improving its economics, and this role owns the product that makes that happen.

This is a product role first. You will own the Express/Mid-prime proposition end to end: who we serve, how we quote and present offers on marketplaces, how the journey converts, how we price, and how the product performs once the loans are on the book. What makes it different from a typical product role is that the product is credit. The levers that drive growth, such as eligibility, pricing, offer design and underwriting, are the same levers that drive loss rates, so you need to be comfortable working with risk and data science rather than handing that part off.

We think this is a great role for someone with around four to five years of experience who has built a strong foundation in lending or fintech, has worked hands-on with data and credit decisioning, and is ready to own a product outright rather than a slice of one. You will set the direction for the segment, run the roadmap, and be accountable for the results, with the backing of experienced risk, data science and commercial leaders around you.

Our decisioning is built on Open Banking and cashflow underwriting rather than credit scores alone. For a higher-APR population acquired through marketplaces, seeing real affordability is what lets us select and price better than the market. The interesting product problem is that richer data comes at a cost to conversion, so the job is to capture that data advantage while designing a journey and offer that customers actually complete.

The defining challenge is balance: scaling volume by an order of magnitude while building a book of genuinely good credit quality. The best people in this space know that those two goals can be reconciled rather than traded off, and are curious enough to work out how.

What you'll be doing

  • Own the Express / Mid-prime product: proposition, roadmap, performance and economics, with direct accountability for the balance between growth and credit quality.

  • Lead how we quote and present offers across aggregator and price-comparison marketplaces, optimising eligibility, risk-based pricing and offer presentation to win the right customers at the point of acquisition.

  • Own conversion through the journey, from quote to disbursal, including how we ask customers for Open Banking data and how that affects drop-off and the quality of the book.

  • Understand and actively manage adverse selection in marketplace-acquired lending, shaping offer, pricing and decisioning strategy to attract the customers we want and screen out the risk we do not.

  • Work with data science to make sure our credit models are calibrated and tuned for this population rather than inherited unchanged from prime or adjacent segments, and be able to get into the data yourself when needed.

  • Use credit and commercial insight to optimise unit economics, balancing approval rates, pricing, loss rates and volume so the product scales profitably.

  • Monitor product and portfolio performance across the customer lifecycle, spotting emerging trends, risks and opportunities early.

  • Shape underwriting strategy, segmentation, credit policy and decisioning logic in partnership with risk and data science.

  • Design and evaluate experiments and strategy changes, and turn the analysis into clear, actionable recommendations.

  • Own the management information for the segment: define the metrics, monitoring and reporting that let the business make consistent decisions about the product.

  • Assess new initiatives, customer segments and product changes with both a commercial and a credit lens.

  • Present clear, structured updates on product performance to senior leadership and governance forums, and support funding and due diligence conversations where the product is in focus.

Who you are

  • A product person at heart: you care about the customer, the journey and the commercial outcome, and you want to own something end to end.

  • Quantitative and hands-on. You are comfortable in SQL and Python (or similar), you can interrogate a dataset yourself, and you can hold your own in a conversation with data scientists about model performance and calibration.

  • Credit-literate. You understand how eligibility, pricing and underwriting decisions shape the book you end up with, and you have a working understanding of adverse selection and why it matters in marketplace lending.

  • Commercially sharp, with a solid grasp of unit economics and a clear understanding that product decisions in lending have to work for both growth and portfolio performance.

  • Curious about trade-offs rather than defensive about them: alert to the fact that deeper affordability assessment can hurt conversion, and motivated by the challenge of capturing its value without sacrificing growth.

  • Able to move between detail and direction: happy getting into the data on a Tuesday and shaping the roadmap on a Wednesday.

  • Confident challenging assumptions and turning analysis into practical action, and able to explain your reasoning clearly to people who are not analysts.

  • Collaborative and credible with risk, commercial, engineering and data science teams.

  • Structured, proactive and comfortable in a scaling environment where priorities evolve quickly and ownership is expected.

Experience and background

  • Around four to five years of experience in product, credit strategy, analytics or a closely related role within consumer lending or fintech. We are deliberately targeting this level: this is a step-up role for someone ready to own a product, not a lateral move for someone who has run several.

  • Experience in unsecured consumer lending, ideally Unsecured Personal Loans (UPL), with exposure to the mechanics of acquiring customers through price-comparison or aggregator marketplaces. Direct experience in higher-APR or near-prime lending is a strong plus but not a prerequisite.

  • Hands-on data skills: SQL as a minimum, and ideally Python or R for analysis. You do not need to be a data scientist, but you need to be able to work alongside them as a peer and do your own analysis.

  • Experience working with or alongside credit decisioning, scorecards or risk models, and an understanding of how they are built, monitored and adjusted for a specific population.

  • Some experience of pricing, eligibility or offer design, and of using experiments or A/B tests to evaluate changes.

  • A track record of using analysis to influence decisions, not just to report on outcomes, in a role where you had some accountability for commercial results.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present clearly to senior stakeholders.

  • Experience with Open Banking data or cashflow underwriting is a plus, as is experience in a fast-growing fintech.

What we offer:

  • Everyone owns a piece of the company - equity

  • Hybrid with 3 days a week in the office

  • 25 days’ holiday a year, plus 8 bank holidays

  • 2 paid volunteering days per year

  • One month paid sabbatical after 4 years

  • Employee loan

  • Free gym membership

  • Team wellness budget to be active together - set up a yoga class, a tennis lesson or go bouldering

Nice to have

  • German language skills

jobs.title: Technical Product Owner mit Entwickler-Background 100 % (w/m/d)
jobs.description:
Das sind wir

Die One of One Group GmbH vereint mit der YOU MAWO GmbH und Additive Scale GmbH führende Unternehmen im Bereich digitaler, maßgefertigter Eyewear und additiver Fertigung. Wir entwickeln und produzieren individuell angepasste Brillen auf Basis präziser 3D-Modelle und datengetriebener Prozesse. Dabei verbinden wir Design, eigene Softwarelösungen und industrielle additive Fertigung zu einer skalierbaren Plattform für Product Customization.

Wir suchen ab sofort für unseren Standort: München, Konstanz, Berlin oder remote in Deutschland

Deine Mission

Du hast selbst Software entwickelt und willst jetzt mitbestimmen, was gebaut wird und warum, ohne den Bezug zum Wie zu verlieren. Als Technical Product Owner verbindest du Business-Anforderungen und technische Umsetzung. Mit deinem agilen Entwicklerteam sprichst du auf Augenhöhe: Du diskutierst Lösungsansätze und triffst technische Richtungsentscheidungen selbst.

Du startest in einem eingespielten Umfeld. Unsere Entwicklungs- und Release-Prozesse funktionieren, und für die Makro-Architektur gibt es einen Software-Architekten. Deine Ideen für Verbesserungen sind jedoch immer willkommen. Deine Energie fließt in Produkt, Technik und KI-Innovation.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Product Ownership & Backlog: Du hast Verantwortung für das Product Backlog, schreibst präzise User Stories und priorisiert Features. Dabei wägst du schnellen Business-Value (Time-to-Market) und technische Qualität (Tech-Debt) bewusst und begründet gegeneinander ab.

  • Technische Entscheidungen auf Augenhöhe: Innerhalb der vorgegebenen Makro-Architektur (GCP, Microservices) gestaltest du das „Wie” im Detail mit, zum Beispiel API-Design, Datenstrukturen, Payloads, Frontend/Backend- Kommunikation und Komponentenschnitt. Du entscheidest selbst oder erarbeitest Lösungen gemeinsam mit den Entwicklern.

  • KI-Integration & Produktinnovation: Du bewertest, wo Generative AI, LLMs und Machine Learning unseren Produkten echten Mehrwert bringen. Diese Features bringst du pragmatisch und nutzerzentriert in unsere bestehenden Systeme.

  • Schnittstelle & Übersetzer: Du arbeitest eng mit dem Software-Architekt, Entwickler Team, Produktmanagement und Geschäftsführung zusammen und übersetzt zwischen diesen Welten.

  • Prozesse weiterentwickeln: Du bringst Impulse ein, um bewährte Abläufe gezielt zu verbessern.

Dein Profil

  • Entwickler-Background (Muss): Du hast mehrere Jahre praktisch als Softwareentwickler gearbeitet, idealerweise im Web-Umfeld (z. B. Java, Python oder Angular).

  • Produkt-Erfahrung: Du hast erste Erfahrung als (Technical) Product Owner, Tech Lead mit Produktverantwortung oder Product-Minded Engineer im agilen Umfeld.

  • Ausbildung: Du hast Informatik, Wirtschaftsinformatik oder ein vergleichbares Fach studiert, oder du bringst einen gleichwertigen Werdegang aus der Praxis mit.

  • Tech-Stack: Du kennst dich in einem Teil unseres Stacks aus und kannst dich in den Rest nach Bedarf einarbeiten: GCP, Microservices, Docker, Kafka, Angular, Java, Python, MySQL, Apache/Tomcat, Jenkins, Bitbucket Pipelines.

  • KI-Mindset: Du interessierst dich ernsthaft für KI in Produkten und willst Modelle in die Produktion bringen, nicht nur in Demos zeigen.

  • Arbeitsweise: Du bist Stratege mit Hands-on-Mentalität und lösungsorientiert. Du erklärst komplexe Themen verständlich, triffst Entscheidungen und vertrittst sie gut begründet.

  • Sprachen: Du sprichst fließend Englisch.

Benefits

  • Unternehmen, in dem du deine Ideen voll einbringen kannst

  • Gutes Betriebsklima in einem aufgeschlossenem, coolen Team

  • Eine verantwortungsvolle und abwechslungsreiche Tätigkeit

  • Zeitarbeitskonto aber keine Überstundenfabrik

  • Eine intensive Einarbeitung und Kolleginnen, die dir gern mit Rat und Tat zur Seite stehen

  • Wellpass Firmenfitness

jobs.description:
Ralph baut das Operating System für Wohnimmobilien. Der Markt ist riesig, und er läuft noch größtenteils auf Aktenordnern, Outlook und USB-Sticks. Wir sind der erste AI Property Manager, der auf einem eigenen Operating System läuft, und betreiben Gebäude damit End-to-End. Ralph OS automatisiert Zahlungen, Buchhaltung, Compliance und Kommunikation. AI-Agenten bereiten die Arbeit vor, und unser Team gibt sie frei. Die Hausverwaltung ist unser Einstieg. Das Ziel ist die neue Infrastruktur für die ganze Kategorie, mit Fintech, Versicherung und Finanzierung auf derselben Plattform. Heute verwalten wir über 10.000 Wohneinheiten und wachsen schnell, organisch und durch Zukäufe. Verantwortung bekommst du bei uns früh, und was du baust, nutzen wir direkt im Alltag.

Deine Rolle

Du verstehst, wie Hausverwaltung wirklich funktioniert, und machst daraus Produkte, die unseren Verwalter:innen und Eigentümer:innen die Arbeit spürbar leichter machen. Du setzt dich mit den Menschen zusammen, die täglich mit unseren Workflows arbeiten, findest das Problem hinter dem Problem und treibst die Lösung bis zum Rollout. Da AI die Art, wie Produkte entstehen, gerade schnell verändert, zählt bei uns vor allem, wie schnell du lernst und wie gründlich du Dinge durchdringst.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du verstehst unsere Verwaltungsprozesse im Detail, indem du mit Property Managern und dem Operations-Team arbeitest, und erkennst, wo Workflows an ihre Grenzen stoßen.

  • Du führst neue Features ein und begleitest den Rollout, damit sie im Alltag wirklich genutzt werden.

  • Du definierst die Metriken, die wir verfolgen müssen, und prüfst nach jedem Release, ob ein Problem im Rollout oder im Produkt liegt.

  • Du planst und führst Experimente und Nutzertests durch, mit internen Nutzer:innen ebenso wie mit Eigentümer:innen.

  • Du erkennst Engpässe, entwickelst Lösungsvorschläge und bringst sie in unsere Produkt-Roadmap ein.

  • Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Tech, Geschäftsführung und unserem In-House-Verwalterteam und Input zur Verbesserung unserer Prozesse und Software

Das bringst du mit

  • Berufserfahrung: Mind. 4 Jahre im Produktmanagement oder Erfahrungen in der Beratung

  • Strukturierte, analytische Denkweise: Du gehst Probleme von Grund auf an und hörst nicht auf, bevor du die Ursache verstanden hast

  • Neugier und Ehrgeiz, dich tief in komplexe Workflows einzuarbeiten, und Lust auf die direkte Arbeit mit deutschsprachigen Operations-Teams

  • Hands-on-Mindset: Du packst an, baust gern Dinge und denkst unternehmerisch

  • Du hörst gut zu, bist empathisch und holst im Gespräch die Informationen heraus, die du brauchst

  • Flexibilität im Kopf: Du passt deine Arbeitsweise an, wenn AI Prozesse verändert

  • Strukturierte Arbeitsweise, hohe Verbindlichkeit und Eigenverantwortung

  • Starkes Kommunikationsvermögen & Offenheit für neue Herausforderungen und digitale Tools

  • Deutsch: C1 oder höher & Englisch: C1 oder höher

Das bieten wir

  • Modernes Setup: MacBook, iPhone und moderne Tools von Tag eins

  • Eigenverantwortliches Arbeiten ohne Mikromanagement

  • Hybrides Arbeiten

  • Urban Sports Club Zuschuss

  • Regelmäßige Team-Events, Team-Lunches und Getränke im Büro

  • Eine Entwicklungsperspektive: Mit dem Wachstum von Ralph kannst du in eine Führungsrolle im Produktbereich hineinwachsen

Bewerbungsprozess

  1. Intro Call (ca. 30 Min.) mit Recruiting

jobs.description:

Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money. We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start:

So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance. We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

Join us if you want to

  1. Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

  2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

About the role

We are looking for a Product Manager to join our Central Operations team and improve how our operational teams serve customers at scale.

Central Operations works across UK and US products to build tools, automation, data capabilities and workflows that make customer service faster, more efficient and more consistent. Current focus areas include complaints, fraud and financial crime, customer contact automation, operational reporting and AI-enabled agent assistance.

This is a highly collaborative role, working closely with Operations, Engineering, Data Science, Product, Risk and Compliance.

  • Define success metrics, monitor performance and use insight to iterate on delivered products.

  • Support controlled trials and pilots before scaling new automation or AI capabilities.

  • Manage dependencies across different product teams, for example integrating motor, loans and cards with a central complaints tool

  • Communicate progress, risks, trade-offs and decisions clearly to senior stakeholders.

What success looks like

  • Operational teams can resolve customer needs faster and with better-quality outcomes.

  • Manual and repetitive casework is reduced through safe, measurable automation.

  • Agents have the information and tools they need at the point of work.

  • Product decisions are grounded in reliable operational data.

  • New capabilities are adopted successfully by frontline teams.

  • Initiatives deliver measurable improvements in service levels, productivity, customer experience or cost efficiency.

What we’re looking for

  • Experience as a Product Manager delivering internal tools, operational products, workflow platforms or automation.

  • Strong understanding of customer operations, contact centres, complaints, servicing or regulated processes.

  • Ability to work effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with an ability to turn data into prioritised action.

  • Experience defining measurable outcomes and using experimentation or pilots to validate solutions.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication.

  • Sound judgement when working with customer data, AI, automation, risk and compliance.

  • A pragmatic, delivery-focused approach, balanced with long-term product thinking.

Desirable experience

  • Experience in financial services, lending, cards, motor finance or another regulated environment.

  • Experience with AI-enabled products, workflow automation or agent-assist tooling.

  • Experience working across multiple markets or product lines.

  • Familiarity with operational metrics such as service level, occupancy, handle time, resolution rate, quality and customer satisfaction.

  • Experience partnering with Data Science, Analytics or Engineering teams.

About the team

The Central Operations team combines Product and Engineering expertise to build tools for Operations. The team includes product managers, engineering leadership and software engineers, and works through shared collaboration channels and cross-functional partnerships.

Why join us?

This role offers the opportunity to work on high-impact products used by operational teams every day, with a direct connection to customer outcomes, colleague experience and business efficiency. You will help shape how Lendable uses technology, data and AI to improve operations across the UK and US.

Life at Lendable

jobs.description:
About us

Rentman is a B2B SaaS scale-up building a smart, powerful operations management platform to support event and media production teams. Our users plan everything from small shoots to massive festivals in 70+ countries, and they all rely on Rentman to keep their gear, people, and timing perfectly in sync. We’re based in Utrecht (NL) with a second office in Toronto (CA), and our 100+ team members work in a culture that’s open, flat, and inclusive, where curiosity drives us, ownership matters, and everyone has the freedom to challenge ideas and make an impact. Check out our public roadmap to see what’s coming next!

Mission of this role

As an interim Senior QA Specialist at Rentman, you make sure every release reaches customers without regressions. You own the test strategy across our 3 product teams and finish moving regression testing from a manual release-day cycle to an automated, shift-left E2E suite. Without this role, quality depends on manual testing on release day, bugs show up in staging or production, and the move to automated testing stalls. This is an interim position: the duration is still to be confirmed, and the role ends once the assignment is complete.

What you'll do

  • Join refinement with the product teams and write Gherkin (Given/When/Then) acceptance specs that developers turn into tests

  • Test new features on staging, going beyond the acceptance criteria to find edge cases, and file clear, reproducible bug reports in Jira

  • Write and review Playwright tests (TypeScript) in the frontend repo, and review developer-written tests in pull requests

  • Monitor the daily automated regression run in GitHub Actions, triage failures the same day, and fix flaky tests at the root cause

  • Run release-day regression and the OWASP ZAP security scan for each release, and give a clear go / no-go call

  • Migrate the remaining legacy tests and decide what is worth automating and what stays manual

  • Organise cross-team QA days and coach developers so they own their tests

     

What we are looking for

  • 5+ years in QA on web applications

  • At least 2 years writing and maintaining UI test automation in code (Playwright, Cypress or Selenium, ideally TypeScript/JavaScript), not only record-and-play tools

  • Strong manual and exploratory testing, with bug reports developers can act on without follow-up questions

  • You have defined a test strategy (what to automate, what to test manually, coverage), not only executed test cases

  • Experience running automated tests in CI (GitHub Actions or similar)

  • You get developers to adopt new habits through pairing, good examples and clear specs, not by policing

     

Nice to haves

  • Experience with complex B2B SaaS

  • Playwright specifically, and Gherkin / BDD

  • Experience leading a shift-left change or coaching developers to own their tests

  • API testing (REST, Postman or similar)

  • Basic security testing (e.g. OWASP ZAP)

What you’ll get

  • Competitive salary based on experience, plus 8% holiday allowance

  • A results-based bonus based on company performance (up to a full 13th month's salary)

  • 25 vacation days to recharge

  • Earn an extra day of PTO for each year at Rentman, from your second anniversary up to five years.

  • A 4-week paid sabbatical after 5 years to go on an adventure

  • Flexible WFH policy & work from anywhere for 4 weeks a year

  • Pension plan through BrightPensioen

  • An annual training budget to grow your skills

  • Access to OpenUp for mental well-being and personal growth

  • Your choice of a shiny new Windows, Linux, or Mac

  • An OV Business card if you live more than 10km from the office

  • An ambitious, inclusive, and diverse international team

  • A flexible, energizing workplace with free lunches, office perks (PS5, ping pong, D&D), legendary karaoke nights, and regular team activities

  • An amazing office in the heart of Utrecht, in the historic Drift 17

jobs.title: Projectmanager
jobs.description:
Met de Xpert Suite bieden ze bij Otherside at Work dé softwareoplossing op het gebied van duurzame inzetbaarheid en sociale zekerheid. Naast toonaangevende organisaties, werken veel arbodiensten en volmachtbedrijven met hun software. Je werk als Project Manager betekent dat je verantwoordelijk bent voor het op tijd, binnen budget én naar volle tevredenheid van alle stakeholders opleveren van hun implementatietrajecten bij klanten. Drie uitdagingen die jij natuurlijk graag aangaat. Het is dan ook jouw aard om altijd een beetje meer te geven dan de klant en je collega’s verwachten.

Taken

In deze super veelzijdige functie ben jij niet alleen het al-ziend-oog met betrekking tot het implementeren van hun software, maar denk jij ook mee met de software ontwikkeling en wensen van de klant. Jouw eigenschap dat je goed overzicht kan houden is handig, want je hebt meestal meerdere projecten tegelijk. Als de situatie daar om vraagt, ben jij in staat om een maatwerkaanpak voor jouw project te bedenken. Jij weet als geen ander het overzicht te behouden, prioriteiten te stellen en de klant tevreden te stellen met hun nieuwe oplossing. Nog niet genoeg uitdaging? We zijn ons internationaal aan het plaatsen, dus wie weet ga je ook in andere landen aan de slag.

Uiteraard ben je communicatief een kei. Je weet andere te inspireren en ben je in staat om de consultants en keyusers topprestaties te laten leveren (niet dat ze dat nog niet doen). Je vindt het leuk om creatieve en innovatieve oplossingen te bedenken die je samen met het projectteam bij de klant voorstelt. Je weet welke risico’s er komen kijken bij het uitrollen van dit soort projecten en hebt dan ook overal een passende, creatieve oplossing voor.

Doordat je al vanaf het sales traject aansluit bij de nieuwe klant kan je goed anticiperen op het project. Jij laat je dan ook niet uit het veld laat slaan als het even niet zo gaat als gehoopt, maar juist dan stroop je je mouwen op, breng je de juiste mensen bij elkaar en zorg je ervoor dat het ultieme doel bereikt wordt: een tevreden klant.

Doordat jij in control bent, kunnen de consultants hun werk beter doen. Ze weten wat er van hen verwacht wordt en hoe ze de klanten blij kunnen maken. Samenwerking, openheid en eerlijkheid en het managen van verwachtingen is hierin key. Een lolletje op zijn tijd en een goed gevoel voor humor doet de rest.

Vereisten

  • In het bezit van een HBO / WO diploma
  • Je hebt minimaal 5 jaar ervaring in een vergelijkbare functie bij een software leverancier;

  • Je ben een enthousiaste doelgerichte teamspeler, waardoor zowel het projectteam als de klant jou graag ziet;

  • Uitstekende communicatieve vaardigheden en goed in schriftelijk vastlegging;
  • Je kunt je vloeiend uitdrukken in het Nederlands en Engels, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk;

Deze eisen en vaardigheden geven een richting van het profiel dat wij zoeken voor deze functie. Voldoe jij niet aan alle eisen en vaardigheden maar denk je wel dat dit de functie voor jou is? Dan nodigen wij je graag uit om te solliciteren.

Benefits

Enthousiast?

jobs.title: Commercial Lead - Clinical Trials
jobs.description:
We’re Heidi.

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. Our platform has absorbed the administrative chaos of 175 million patient visits and supported 67 million clinical hours. Today, we support 2.8 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries, in 110 languages and over 200 specialties.

Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s capacity for care and strengthen the human connection at its heart.

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

We’ve grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years.

To go further, we’ve secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund.

If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in.

The role

We are hiring a Clinical Trials Lead to own the commercial work that follows. You will develop Heidi’s view of the market, identify the strongest entry point, build senior relationships across the industry, secure early customers and shape a repeatable route to market. Your knowledge of clinical trials will inform and shape what Heidi builds.

This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who operates like a founder. You will make the calls, open the doors, write the proposal, run the meeting and stay accountable after the contract is signed. As the business proves itself, the role can grow into broader ownership of Heidi’s clinical trials business.

What you’ll do

  • Develop the market thesis. Map the clinical trials ecosystem, test the most valuable opportunities and recommend where Heidi should focus its time and capital.

  • Lead customer development. Build direct relationships with senior decision makers across sponsors, biotechnology companies, CROs, sites and health systems. Conduct the outreach yourself and turn conversations into qualified opportunities.

  • Own early commercial outcomes. Build the pipeline, secure design partners and paid programmes, and own early revenue. Define the measures that show whether the business is gaining traction.

  • Shape the proposition. Turn buyer needs into a clear commercial offer, including target customer, value proposition, pricing, packaging and proof of value.

  • Inform what Heidi builds. Bring evidence from customers and clinical trials workflows to the product lead. Help the team choose problems worth solving while the product lead retains ownership of product strategy and delivery.

  • Navigate the buying process. Understand how life sciences organisations evaluate vendors, allocate budgets, manage procurement and compliance, and move from pilot to broader deployment.

  • Build the delivery model. Work with product, engineering, clinical, legal and implementation colleagues to make early programmes successful and increasingly repeatable.

  • Create the route to scale. Determine which partnerships, channels, proof points and team capabilities are required to grow beyond founder-led selling.

  • Represent Heidi. Build Heidi’s credibility with customers, partners and industry networks through thoughtful engagement and useful domain expertise.

What you’ll need

The strongest candidates will combine deep clinical trials knowledge with a record of creating commercial value. We expect the following experience.

  • Deep experience in the clinical trials industry through a pharmaceutical or biotechnology company, CRO, trial technology business, research network or closely related organisation.

  • A strong understanding of how clinical trials are funded, sold, bought and delivered, including the incentives and constraints faced by sponsors, CROs and research sites.

  • A record of building revenue, partnerships, a business line or a company in the sector. You can show what you personally originated and how it performed.

  • Senior commercial credibility. You can open a conversation with an industry executive, diagnose the underlying business problem and move the relationship towards a concrete commitment.

  • The judgement to operate in a regulated environment while respecting Good Clinical Practice, patient consent, privacy and data integrity.

  • The independence to create structure, make decisions and produce results without an established playbook or a large supporting team.

  • Passion for AI, shown through hands-on building, prototyping, or side projects.

  • You default to building over requesting.

  • You're confident in your thinking and open to being wrong. Great ideas win regardless of who surfaces them.

How we show up

  • Build for the next decade, not next quarter. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.

  • Lead, don't wait. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.

  • Follow the evidence. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.

  • Own the outcome. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.

  • Ship, measure, go again. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.

  • Live in clinicians' reality. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.

Why Heidi?

You’ll join a team measured on real-world impact, not press cycles. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders and designers who’ve felt (on every side of the equation) what non-care feels like, the moral and practical toll as a provider or receiver.

Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. Standard tech playbooks routinely fail in healthcare, and the friction of the medical system will test your perseverance. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose a purpose-driven mission that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognize that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it.

True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

We take care of you.

We offer comprehensive private medical and dental cover through Bupa, 24/7 mental health, coaching and wellbeing support through Sonder, a £100/month Healthy Heidi's wellness stipend, a £500 home office budget, a £700 annual learning and development budget, 26 weeks paid primary parental leave and 18 weeks paid secondary parental leave, fertility support up to £7,000, up to four weeks of work from anywhere per year, Recharge Days after major milestones and busy periods, 10 days per year of clinical leave for eligible clinical roles, and a hybrid working environment with 3 days in the office.

We chose to open-source our benefits hub, if you care to take a peek.

We're the team behind Back Market's Trade-in program, the system that lets customers exchange their old devices for cash toward their next refurbished purchase. It's a win-win-win: customers get more purchasing power, refurbishers get quality supply, and the planet gets a break from unnecessary e-waste.

To achieve this, our team is made up of seven engineers, an engineering manager and a product manager collaborating closely with designers, data analysts, operations and business partners.
